questions.question: What does JSX compile into?
options: Calls that create plain JavaScript objects describing elements
questions.explanation: JSX compiles to createElement calls (or the modern jsx runtime), which return plain objects describing the UI. Nothing touches the DOM at that point.

questions.question: What does this render when items is an empty array?
questions.explanation: `items.length` is 0, which is falsy, so `&&` returns 0 - and 0 is a number React happily renders. Compare with `> 0` to avoid it.

questions.question: Which of these can NOT go directly inside JSX curly braces?
questions.explanation: Braces hold expressions. `if` is a statement, so compute the value above the return or use a ternary instead.

questions.question: Why does JSX use className instead of class?
options: React styles work differently from CSS
class is a reserved word in JavaScript, and JSX attributes become object properties
It is required by the HTML specification
questions.explanation: JSX attributes become properties of a JavaScript object, and `class` is reserved. The same reason turns `for` into `htmlFor`.

questions.question: What does the style prop expect?
options: A CSS string such as "color: red"
An object with camelCased property names
A reference to a stylesheet file
questions.explanation: `style` takes an object, for example `{{ color: "red", fontSize: 16 }}`. The outer braces are the JSX expression and the inner braces are the object.

questions.question: Why would you use a fragment instead of a wrapper div?
options: Fragments render faster than any element
Fragments group children without adding a node to the DOM
Fragments allow multiple root elements to be returned as separate values
questions.explanation: A fragment groups children so a component can return one value, without producing a DOM element that could break table, grid or flex layouts.

questions.question: Render a list heading and items without a wrapper element
questions.explanation: A fragment lets a component return several siblings while keeping the DOM clean.

editor.title: Return a fragment
editor.instructions: Return an h4 saying 'Colours' followed by a ul containing three li elements: Red, Green, Blue.

tests.name: The heading reads 'Colours'
tests.code: var el = document.querySelector('#root h4'); return !!el && el.textContent.trim() === 'Colours';

tests.name: The items are Red, Green and Blue
tests.code: var items = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('#root ul li')).map(function (n) { return n.textContent.trim(); }); return items.join(',') === 'Red,Green,Blue';
